ecsCoresOf: {cores} CPU(s) of {of}, as the ECS agent measured it
ecsCores: {cores} CPU(s), as the ECS agent measured it
utilisationWhy: {cores} of {of} CPU(s) over {seconds} s, {sampled, select, fresh {two samples taken for this page} other {since the previous page}}
cpuTimeWhy: every process of the container since it started (user {user} s, system {system} s)
throttledWhy: {pct} of periods, {seconds} s held back by the quota
peak: ; the most it has used is {peak}
anonymousWhy: the processes' own memory: heaps, stacks, buffers
pageCacheWhy: files the kernel caches, and gives back under pressure
kernelWhy: the kernel's own structures on the container's behalf
oomKillsWhy: processes the kernel killed at the limit (oom_kill, in memory.events or v1's memory.oom_control)
fromEcsAgent: From the ECS agent, because the cgroup cannot be read: {why}.
workerThreadsWhy: request and hosted-surface workers, threads of the front process
residentWhy: across {n} process(es); a thread's is its process's
ecsCpuWhy: {pct} of the task's vCPUs, between the agent's last two samples
about: The container's CPU and memory are read from its cgroup (v2), each process's and worker thread's from the process or thread itself, when the page is drawn; nothing is kept but the previous CPU sample. Its one control runs a full garbage collection on demand; nothing else here changes anything.
noTotalLimit: no total limit to measure against
collectAll: Collect garbage in every process and worker thread
notCollectable: not this node’s front process or a worker thread of it
gcWarning: A full garbage collection stops the thread it runs in until it finishes, and in the front process that pauses every listener of this node. It is a diagnostic: V8 collects on its own schedule, and memory a forced collection does not free is held, not garbage. Each press is audited.
gcResultSummary: {n} isolate(s) collected, {freed} freed in all, the longest pause {pause} ms. The table below was read before the collection; reload the page to read it again.
